Subject: GitHub integration questions + demo request

Hi Monica,

We just signed up for Redwood via the self-serve flow and are exploring the GitHub integration for a bot that comments on PRs and annotates failures. A few quick questions before booking a demo: 

- Do you support GitHub Apps (recommended) or only OAuth apps?
- For private repos, what scopes are required and can we limit installation to a single org repo?
- How does webhook delivery behave at scale (retries, dedupe, replay)? Any rate-limit guidance?
- Does Redwood persist installation tokens or do you proxy webhooks without storing tokens?

We'd love a short demo focused on the integration flow and webhook payloads. I’m on PT (San Francisco) and available Tue/Wed afternoons. Can you recommend a 30-minute slot?

Thanks,
Priya
Product Lead, RepoHelpers Inc.
priya@repohelpers.io

Hi Priya — great to meet you and welcome, glad you tried the self-serve flow. I looped in Karthik (our integrations engineer) so he can address the webhook/architecture specifics during the demo. Quick answers up front: 

- We strongly recommend GitHub Apps; they give the most granular install scopes and better security posture.
- For private repos you can limit installation to specific repos or to the org; required scopes are generally: repositories (read), pull_requests (read), and webhooks/events. Karthik can list exact permissions during the call.
- Webhooks: we deliver with exponential backoff and idempotency keys; we persist a short delivery log for replay and troubleshooting. We’ll walk through retry behavior and dedupe guarantees in the demo.
- Tokens: we store installation tokens encrypted with KMS for short lived use (refresh before expiry). No long-term plaintext secrets.

Would 30 minutes on Tue Jul 20 at 2:00pm PT or Wed Jul 21 at 11:00am PT work for you? If neither, share a few slots and I’ll send a calendar invite.

I’ll attach a short pre-demo checklist and a one-pager on the GitHub App flow.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai

Quick prep notes (attached): redwood-github-app-guide.pdf and pre-demo-checklist.md. Highlights below so Rahul can skim: 

- Sample payloads: attached samples for "pull_request.opened" and "check_run.completed" (we’ll walk through filtering by repo and event type).
- Data access: Redwood does not pull full repo contents by default; the GitHub App can be configured to grant only metadata, PR bodies, and check/run contexts. If you explicitly enable content:read we can access files, but that’s an opt-in permission.
- Rate limits: typical production customers design with event batching and lightweight webhook handlers; we’ll share best-practice thresholds in the call.
